reading.body:
Mike Quigley's AI record is dominated by data center power and siting bills, not by model safety or frontier research. Eight of his thirteen dated events are cosponsorships, and six of those eight address where data centers go, what they do to the grid, or what they cost ratepayers.

The pattern runs in one direction. The Responsible Data Center Siting Act, the AI Data Center Site Selection Transparency Act, the Artificial Intelligence Environmental Impacts Act, the Power for the People Act, the SHIELD Act, and the Protecting Families from AI Data Center Energy Costs Act all treat the physical buildout as the thing to govern. Only the FRONTIER Act and the GUARDRAILS Act reach the model layer. The dates cluster: five of the thirteen fall between December 2025 and April 2026, and the newest entry is September 2026.

For AI specifically, this is a legislator whose attention sits where the binding constraint sits. Compute depends on buildings and power, and the bills here are about buildings and power, siting, transmission cost, and environmental review. The single campaign contribution in the record, $2,500 from the Amazon PAC in May 2025, is the only money entry, and it is small enough that it establishes a filing rather than a pattern.

What the data does not show is outcome. Every bill entry carries its latest status date, not a vote or enactment, so nothing here says whether any of these measures advanced. The four recorded votes are on suspension motions, which the record does not tie to the cosponsorships. The page also draws no causal link between the contribution and any bill, and the data cannot support one.

summary: Every dated AI event this site holds for Mike Quigley: bills sponsored or cosponsored, recorded votes on AI bills, and money from AI company and AI-focused political committees, newest first. 13 events.
